# Bitcoin Rainbow: full page text

> Full text and data facts from https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/
> Bitcoin Rainbow is a free site in plain words. It tells what bitcoin is, shows where the price sits next to its own past growth, and makes the author's case for the long run, crashes shown plainly.
> Its tools only measure: chart explorers for any day since 2010, a what-if-you'd-bought calculator, a replay of small weekly buys, and a model explorer, all on real past prices. No ads. No accounts.
> Past prices: blockchain.info. Live price: Coinbase.
> Facts below are as of Oct 31, 2026, unless a date is shown. Live facts change each day. Since Nov 1, 2026 the homepage also carries live computed gauges (RSI, Mayer Multiple, the 50/200-day lines, drawdown, swing size), network readings (halving clock, supply issued, hashrate, fees, Fear and Greed, dominance), a tap-a-crash explorer, a model explorer with the model's track record, and a daily read kept at /analysis, all computed from the same public data, none of it financial advice.
> That is the past. Not a promise.

## Home (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/)

The Bitcoin Rainbow.
Sixteen years of bitcoin's price on one chart, in plain words.

Screen one shows today's fact: the price, the band it sits in, and how far it sits from its long-run line. A slider under the chart picks any day since 2010 and shows that day's price, its band, and the year that came next. The full chart, with the band list, is in Chapter 1.

The page is five chapters, each one a question.

### Chapter 1: Where does the price sit in its long story?

What bitcoin is: Bitcoin is money for the internet. No company runs it, and no boss can print more: only 21 million will ever exist. It lives on many computers at once. You can own a whole coin, or a small piece.

It is a growth chart for bitcoin's price. Through the middle runs one line: bitcoin's long-run growth, fit to every daily price on record. Around the line stack nine colored bands, Deep Blue at the bottom, Red at the top. The low bands mean the price sits far under its own past growth. The high bands mean far over it. A Reddit user, azop, drew the first rainbow in 2014, on a growth line by trolololo, a forum user. Blockchain Center made the chart famous. The line here is our own fit of the same public prices. That is the past. Not a promise.

Think of the marks on a wall for a child. The chart does the same for price. One line shows the growth path. Bands sit above and below the line.

Tap a band in the list and the page tells you how far from the line that band sits, how many days the price has lived there, and what the next year did after past visits.

The chapter ends with a model explorer: pick how far out (1, 5, or 10 years) and which line the price follows (the bottom band, the growth line, or the top band), and see the model's own lines stretched forward. Not a forecast.

### How the chart is made

- The line is fit to all past prices with least squares.
- The rainbow chart is a public chart: azop drew the first one in 2014, on trolololo's growth line, and Blockchain Center made it famous. This line is this site's own fit, on the same public prices.
- The line is: ln(price) = -37.283 + 5.597 x ln(days since Jan 3, 2009).
- Jan 3, 2009 is day one. It is the day the first block was made.
- The fit uses 5,917 days with a price above zero.
- Those days run from Aug 18, 2010 to Oct 29, 2026.
- There are 9 bands. Each band is 0.3 wide in log space.
- The line sits in the third band from the base. The base of the bands is the line times 0.47. The top is the line times 7.03.
- Band names are colors only. Old charts used names that told you to buy or sell. This site does not.

### The 9 bands on Oct 31, 2026

Each row shows the price range for that band on Oct 31, 2026, and the share of all past days that sat in that band.

- Deep Blue: $67,007 to $90,449. 23.2% of days. 36% to 53% under the line.
- Blue: $90,449 to $122,094. 16.3% of days. 14% to 36% under the line.
- Sky: $122,094 to $164,810. 13.4% of days. Hugs the line, 14% under to 16% over.
- Green: $164,810 to $222,470. 14.0% of days. 16% to 57% over the line.
- Lime: $222,470 to $300,303. 7.3% of days. 57% over, up to about double.
- Yellow: $300,303 to $405,366. 6.8% of days. About 2 to 3 times the line.
- Orange: $405,366 to $547,187. 4.5% of days. About 3 to 4 times the line.
- Dark Orange: $547,187 to $738,625. 1.8% of days. About 4 to 5 times the line.
- Red: $738,625 to $997,040. 1.6% of days. About 5 to 7 times the line.
- 597 days sat below all bands. 57 days sat above all bands.

### Two points marked on the chart

- 2021 top: $67,562 (Nov 9, 2021 close in this data set).
- 2022 low: $15,760 (Nov 22, 2022 close in this data set).

### Chapter 2: What happened the other times it sat here?

Every day, on one chart: a second explorer over every daily close, with the bands, the 50-day and 200-day lines, and the halvings marked. Scrub to any day to see its price, its band, and the year that came next.

- The home page shows every daily close, Aug 18, 2010 to Oct 29, 2026. Last close in that set: $81,275 on Oct 29, 2026.
- Falls of 40% or more, top to bottom, in that set: 2011 crash, down 93.2%. The 2013 to 2015 fall, down 84.9%. The 2018 fall, down 83.2%. The 2021 to 2022 fall, down 76.7%.
- The fall from the Oct 7, 2025 top ($124,777) is still open in that set. Its low so far there: $58,534 on Jul 1, 2026, down 53.1%.
- A share card on the home page shows the worst, middle, and best ten-year paths. Its line: "That is the past. Not a promise."

What if you'd bought? Pick a day and a sum, and the tool shows what that buy is worth at the last close. From the record: $1,000 on Dec 5, 2013 bought 0.8796 bitcoin, worth $71,489 at the Oct 29, 2026 close. No fees or taxes counted. That is the past. Not a promise.

The plain chart: the same prices with no colors and no bands, plus the 50-day and 200-day averages, and the ceiling and floor levels the price keeps meeting.

The gauges: six readings computed from the same daily prices. Heat over the last two weeks (RSI). Price vs its 200-day average (the Mayer Multiple). The trend lines. How far the price sits from its top. The daily swing. And the price vs the rainbow line.

A little, every week: like an allowance, in reverse.

This is called DCA. It means you buy a set sum on a set day, week by week.

Pick an amount: $10, $25, $50, or $100 a week.
Pick a span: 1, 3, or 5 years.
See the past: the tool buys once a week at the real close near that day. It adds up the coins. It values them at the live price.

Results as of Oct 31, 2026 (live price $77,471). Past only.

- $10 a week, 1 year, 53 buys: put in $530. Worth $542.
- $25 a week, 1 year, 53 buys: put in $1,325. Worth $1,355.
- $50 a week, 1 year, 53 buys: put in $2,650. Worth $2,710.
- $100 a week, 1 year, 53 buys: put in $5,300. Worth $5,420.
- $10 a week, 3 years, 157 buys: put in $1,570. Worth $1,684.
- $25 a week, 3 years, 157 buys: put in $3,925. Worth $4,210.
- $50 a week, 3 years, 157 buys: put in $7,850. Worth $8,420.
- $100 a week, 3 years, 157 buys: put in $15,700. Worth $16,839.
- $10 a week, 5 years, 261 buys: put in $2,610. Worth $4,712.
- $25 a week, 5 years, 261 buys: put in $6,525. Worth $11,779.
- $50 a week, 5 years, 261 buys: put in $13,050. Worth $23,559.
- $100 a week, 5 years, 261 buys: put in $26,100. Worth $47,118.

That is the past. Not a promise.

Today's read closes the chapter: a short daily analysis written only from the numbers on the page. Past reads are kept at /analysis.

### Chapter 3: Is Bitcoin itself healthy?

The network itself, in numbers the network reports. The halving clock: how far the blocks stand between the last halving (Apr 20, 2024) and the next one. Coins already out, of the 21 million that will ever exist. Computing power (hashrate): quintillions of guesses per second, spent guarding the ledger. Fees right now: what one payment pays to jump the line. Fear & Greed: a 0-to-100 mood score for the whole market, the Fear & Greed Index by Alternative.me, shown with its maker's name next to the number. Bitcoin's share of the whole crypto market's value, counted by CoinGecko.

### Chapter 4: Why did it crash those times?

Tap a crash: seven big falls, each drawn from the daily prices, with its top, its bottom, its size, and its story. One table holds all seven: the top, the bottom, the fall, the days down, and the days back to the top, all measured from the same daily closes. The top is a daily close; the fall runs to the lowest daily close after it; days back to the top counts to the first close at or above the top again. Daily closes can miss a swing inside one day, so a fall here can read smaller than the worst hour of it.

Six of the seven have named causes on the page, from the Mt. Gox hack and collapse, to China's bank and mining bans, the ICO mania bursting, the Terra/Luna and FTX contagion, and the 2021 Tesla reversal. The newest fall, 2025 to now, down 53% so far, is still unfolding. The record so far names no single cause for it, and the site says so rather than inventing one.

It swings hard. We could be wrong: since 2011, it fell by half or more. Seven times. In 2022, it fell by about three fourths. It can do that again. A total loss should sting, not sink you.

It could fall and stay down. New laws could hurt it. The climb is a pattern, not a law. Many fans keep 5 to 10 in 100 saved. The bold end is 10 to 20 in 100. Only money you will not need for years. This is learning, not financial advice.

### Chapter 5: How do we know any of this?

Sources & method. The model: rainbow model, our own fit, version 1. ln(price) = -37.28 + 5.60 x ln(days since Jan 3, 2009). Fit window Aug 18, 2010 to Oct 29, 2026: 5,917 daily closes. Fit score (R-squared): 0.96, in log terms. That score grades how well the line hugs the past. It says nothing about next year.

Where each part comes from: the chart, the gauges, and the falls use daily closes from blockchain.info, the full record since 2010; the live price is from Coinbase. The network numbers (block height, hashrate, fees) come from mempool.space; supply is checked against blockchain.info. Fear & Greed is the Fear & Greed Index by Alternative.me. Bitcoin's share comes from CoinGecko.

What to watch for: prices here are daily closes. A swing inside one day can be bigger than the day shows. In June 2011, one exchange flashed to one cent for a few minutes. The daily closes say that fall was 93%. Both are true, of different things. Bitcoin's share of all crypto depends on who counts the coins; sites disagree by a point or two. The model explorer stretches the model's own lines forward; those lines are labelled as the model's, never as a forecast. When a source is quiet, its card says so instead of showing an old number as new.

The standing line: this is analysis and education, not financial advice. Numbers here are computed from real data and stamped with the day they describe.

### The two ways people hold it

- IBIT: in a stock account, like a stock. You do not hold the coins.
- Exchange app: you hold real bitcoin. You keep the keys.
- Fees: both charge fees. IBIT: yearly. Apps: per buy.

### Learn the words

- Price: price is the tag at the store. It changes every day.
- Technical: watching the line. Up, down, or flat?
- Fundamental: a health check. Strong? Rare? Used a lot? Only 21 million will ever be.

### One year ago

- One year before Oct 31, 2026, the price was $109,553. The past year was down 29.3%. The site calls that down a lot.

## Should I buy bitcoin? (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/should-i-buy-bitcoin)

No chart can answer that, and this site will not try. Two facts from the past: pick any start day, and four years on the price stood higher, for all 4,460 four-year stretches; and the price fell by half or more seven times, worst 93% in 2011. The record is the past, not a promise. The size is the real choice: size it so a total loss stings but does not sink you. Many fans hold 5 to 10 of every 100 saved dollars; the bold end is 10 to 20 in 100. Only money you will not need for years. This is learning, not financial advice.

## Has bitcoin ever lost money over 4 years? (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/has-bitcoin-ever-lost-money-over-4-years)

No, not once so far. All 4,460 four-year stretches from Aug 2010 to Oct 2026 ended higher, and all 2,270 ten-year stretches ended higher. The worst stretch began Apr 9, 2021 at $58,049 and ended four years on at $76,267, about a third higher. The middle can still hurt: buy at the Dec 2017 top ($19,280) and the price was $3,232 one year on, a fall of 83%, before ending four years on at $47,658. "So far" is part of the answer. That is the past, not a promise.

## What happens after bitcoin crashes? (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/what-happens-after-bitcoin-crashes)

So far, each big fall ended, and the price climbed back to its old top in about two to three years. The four biggest: 2011, $34 to $2, down 93%, back in about 2 years; 2013 to 2015, $1,137 to $172, down 85%, back in about 3 years; 2017 to 2018, $19,280 to $3,232, down 83%, back in about 3 years; 2021 to 2022, $67,562 to $15,760, down 77%, back in about 2 years. Comebacks are not straight lines: after the spring 2021 low of $29,790, the price was lower a year on, at $23,227. The newest fall is still open: the top was Oct 2025 at $124,777, the price fell 53% to $58,534 by Jul 2026, and sat near $81,000 at the end of Oct 2026. No fall is owed an ending. This is learning, not financial advice.

## The bitcoin crash of 2018 (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/bitcoin-crash-2018)

Bitcoin topped at $19,280 on Dec 17, 2017, then fell for a year. By Feb 6, 2018 it was $6,925, down 64%. The low was $3,232 on Dec 16, 2018, down 83%, 364 days after the top. The price first closed above the old top on Dec 1, 2020, at $19,710: 1,080 days after the top, about 3 years. This crash ended; no fall is owed an ending. This is learning, not financial advice.

## The bitcoin crash of 2022 (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/bitcoin-crash-2022)

Bitcoin topped at $67,562 on Nov 9, 2021, then fell for just over a year. By Jun 19, 2022 it was $18,978, down 72%. The last drop came in Nov 2022, the month the FTX exchange failed. The low was $15,760 on Nov 22, 2022, down 77%, 378 days after the top. The price first closed above the old top on Mar 5, 2024, at $68,378: 847 days after the top, about 2 years and 4 months. This crash ended; no fall is owed an ending. This is learning, not financial advice.

## How long do bitcoin crashes last? (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/how-long-do-bitcoin-crashes-last)

Counted in days from the daily price record: 2011, down 93%, 164 days down, 630 days top to top again; 2013 to 2015, down 85%, 406 days down, 1,177 days top to top again; 2017 to 2018, down 83%, 364 days down, 1,080 days; spring 2021, down 53%, 98 days down, 189 days; 2021 to 2022, down 77%, 378 days down, 847 days. The 2025 fall is still open: down 53% to its low so far, not back at the top. Falls of a fifth to a third happened ten more times and most ended in weeks. This is learning, not financial advice.

## What is a bear market in bitcoin? (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/what-is-a-bitcoin-bear-market)

A bear market is a long, deep fall from a price top; writers often draw the line at 20% down. Since 2011, bitcoin has fallen by half or more seven times: 2011 down 93%, 2013 down 71%, 2013 to 2015 down 85%, 2017 to 2018 down 83%, spring 2021 down 53%, 2021 to 2022 down 77%, and 2025 to now down 53%, still open. A crash is about speed; a bear market is about length. The word names the past; it does not time the next turn. This is learning, not financial advice.

## Privacy (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/privacy)

This site reads public price data. It does not ask for your name. It has no accounts. It sets no tracking cookies of its own. Prices come from Coinbase and blockchain.info. Not advice. Just a picture of the past.

## Terms (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/terms)

This site shows past prices in plain words. It does not give financial advice. It never says buy or sell. Prices can be wrong or late. A price here can be old by the time you read it.
